title: Game Conductors of Finite Groups: Determinantal Torsion from Structured Payoff Probes
summary: We attach to a finite group $G$ and a structured payoff probe $φ$ an integer \emph{payoff-difference lattice} $M_φ(G)$ and its \emph{conductor} $C_φ(G)$: the primes at which $M_φ(G)$ loses rank modulo $p$. Our main result is an exact computation: for any CA-group the commuting conductor is rad$(b-1)$, where $b$ is the number of maximal abelian subgroups. In particular, conductor primes need not divide $|G|$: the prime $3$ occurs for a $2$-group of order $64$ with $b=7$.
